dress_code.men: Modest clothing with shoulders and knees covered (pants, dhotis, or kurtas)
dress_code.women: Sarees, chudidars with dupattas, or modest traditional wear

dos: Remove Footwear: Leave all footwear at the designated counter outside the raised stone platform before stepping onto the temple deck.
Hire a Guide: Use an authorized ASI certified guide near the entrance counter to learn about the history of black basalt carvings and floating bricks.
Explore Nearby Attractions: Combine your visit with a trip to the scenic Ramappa Lake (located 1 km away for boating) or the Ghanpur Group of Temples.
donts: Do Not Touch or Lean on Sculptures: The black basalt Madanika (dancer) statues feature a rare glass-like mirror polish. Leaning on or touching them is strictly prohibited under heritage protection laws.
No Plastic Littering: The entire stone boundary and surrounding gardens are strictly designated as a zero-plastic zone.
Dress Code Violations: Avoid overly revealing outfits. Ensure shoulders and knees are fully covered out of respect for the active place of worship.
